title: Soul Feast #62: Compassion is Not for Cowards
excerpt: Are you making choices in love or fear?
bodyHtml:
Are you making choices in love or fear? Take this self-assessment today to find out.

In this powerful Soul Feast, Gary explores compassion as a living experience rather than a concept. He guides listeners into the inner world where fear and love shape every perception and interaction. Through clear examples, Gary shows how genuine compassion arises only when we are willing to face our own frightened parts of the personality with courage, emotional awareness, and honesty – and how this inner work opens the heart to others in a way no external practice can.

Gary explains why compassion cannot be created through caretaking, sympathy, or trying to “fix” others. Instead, it emerges naturally when we recognize the pain behind another person’s fear-driven behavior by first recognizing it in ourselves. As he walks listeners through the mechanics of frightened and loving parts of the personality, 

Gary reveals how emotional literacy, presence, and authentic power transform the way we relate to ourselves and others.

Ultimately, compassion grows as we develop the courage to feel our own emotional pain directly – without acting on it, repressing it, or projecting it outward. This is the road to authentic power, and it’s the same road that dissolves judgment, softens the heart, and allows love to lead the way.

What You’ll Discover in This Soul Feast:

(01:10) — Why compassion requires courage – and why it cannot be accessed from fear

(03:00) — How emotional awareness helps you recognize fear-based parts of your personality

(06:01) — The moment authentic power is created: choosing love while feeling the pull of fear

(08:40) — Why emotional pain is physical pain – and how this shifts your understanding of inner work

(11:35) — Recognizing fear in others: the key to seeing their pain and dissolving judgment

(13:55) — Why compassion for others begins with compassion for yourself

Embrace the Soul Step Challenge

Take out your Soul Notebook and record every moment you notice yourself contracting in fear –  whether through judgment, irritation, withdrawal, or the impulse to control. Note the physical sensations, the thoughts, and the reactions that arise in those moments. Then write down moments when you felt yourself soften, open, or act from love – even while fear was still present. Observe what changed inside you. At the end of the day or week, review your notes with curiosity, not judgment. Let them show you how often fear or love shaped your experience, and how your heart naturally expands when you choose compassion for yourself and others.
